sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS: the GitLab project https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr and the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/ .
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README give a clear, succinct description of what ssrfr does (a server-side request forgery guard that parses, resolves and classifies each redirect hop once and pins the connection to a validated address): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr#readme
interact_justification: The pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/ explains how to obtain the package (README installation section), links the bug tracker ("Report a bug"), the contributing guide (https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/CONTRIBUTING.html) and the security policy.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains how to report issues and send merge requests on GitLab (the GitHub copy is a read-only mirror), and what a merge request needs: tests for new code, one NEWS.md bullet per user-facing change, and a passing verification command.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements for acceptable contributions: implement only against [ratified] sections of the v1 specification, and pass Rscript scripts/verify.R (lint, NEWS heading, tests with no skips, R CMD check --as-cran) and scripts/check-design.py: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: DESCRIPTION declares License: MIT + file LICENSE, and the LICENSE file (the CRAN MIT template's year and copyright holder) is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: The pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/ carries the README (installation and use) and the introduction vignette (https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/articles/introduction.html); the normative contract is the v1 specification: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/design/specs/ssrfr-v1.md
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function is documented with roxygen2 man pages, published as the reference at https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/reference/ .
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available on GitLab: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr
version_unique_justification: ssrfr has not been released yet. The development version carries the DESCRIPTION Version 0.0.0.9000, and the release checklist in CONTRIBUTING.md sets a new X.Y.Z for each release, which CRAN refuses to accept twice: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning, with R's .9000 suffix for development versions (0.0.0.9000 today): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
version_tags_justification: No release has been made yet, so there are no version tags; the release checklist in CONTRIBUTING.md requires tagging each released commit vX.Y.Z: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md records every user-facing change and becomes the release notes for the first release; ssrfr has not been released yet: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab work items serve as the public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items), linked as "Report a bug" on the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/ssrfr/ . DESCRIPTION names the same tracker as BugReports by its legacy /-/issues address, the form R's CRAN incoming check requires.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed on the public tracker to date (0 issues on 2026-10-03), so none is unacknowledged: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been filed on the public tracker to date (0 issues on 2026-10-03), so none is unanswered: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: GitLab Issues provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items/?state=all
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in the security policy, linked from the README: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md . Reports go to the maintainer by email, with a confidential GitLab issue as a documented alternative; it also states what is in and out of scope.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md) documents two confidential channels: email to bartek@turczynski.pl, and a GitLab issue submitted with "This issue is confidential" ticked, visible only to the reporter, assignees and project members allowed to see confidential issues.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received through GitLab in the last 6 months (0 issues, confidential ones included, on 2026-10-03); SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a report within 7 days: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools); pure R, no compiled code: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling.
build_floss_tools_justification: R and its toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_justification: Automated test suite using testthat (edition 3) and cucumber feature specs, with a conformance corpus, local loopback HTTP/TLS servers and no live network: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with testthat::test_local() or devtools::test(), and as part of R CMD check; the full gate is Rscript scripts/verify.R: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/scripts/verify.R
test_most_justification: covr measures coverage in the coverage CI job on every push to main and reports it through GitLab's coverage reporting; the main pipeline of 2026-10-03 measured 98.8% line coverage: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/jobs/16912959506
test_policy_justification: AGENTS_LANG.md, the R conventions contributors follow, states "New code requires tests" and that a skipped test fails the gate (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/AGENTS_LANG.md); the v1 specification requires each load-bearing safety invariant to be encoded as a test: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/design/specs/ssrfr-v1.md
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality and fixes ship with tests; recent behavioral commits on main (e.g. the xn-- A-label refusal, the non-ASCII wire-string refusal) each add or change tests/testthat files: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/commits/main
tests_documented_added_justification: The test requirement is written in AGENTS_LANG.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/AGENTS_LANG.md), not in CONTRIBUTING.md, the instructions for change proposals (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
warnings_justification: lintr and R CMD check --as-cran surface warnings in scripts/verify.R (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/scripts/verify.R), which runs as the pre-push hook and in the verify CI job on every push to main (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml).
warnings_fixed_justification: scripts/verify.R fails on any lint and on any R CMD check ERROR, WARNING or NOTE not explicitly allowed with a written reason, so warnings are fixed before a push lands.
warnings_strict_justification: scripts/verify.R fails on any lintr finding, any R CMD check WARNING, and any NOTE outside a short allow-list whose every entry carries a reason: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/scripts/verify.R
know_secure_design_justification: ssrfr is a security control designed from a written threat model: parse once, resolve once, classify every address, pin the connection to a validated address, fail closed on anything undetermined, and never weaken certificate verification; its invariants are in the v1 specification: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/design/specs/ssrfr-v1.md
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the SSRF bypass classes (alternate IP spellings, DNS rebinding between check and connect, parser differentials between checker and transport, redirect-borne credential leaks, proxy and ambient-environment overrides, decompression bombs) and maps each to an invariant with a test: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/design/specs/ssrfr-v1.md
crypto_published_justification: ssrfr implements no cryptography; its only cryptographic protocol is TLS for https, performed by libcurl's TLS backend. TLS is a published, publicly reviewed protocol.
crypto_call_justification: ssrfr re-implements no cryptography: https is delegated to libcurl (through the curl R package) and its TLS backend.
crypto_floss_justification: The cryptography ssrfr relies on (TLS through libcurl, e.g. with OpenSSL) is implementable with FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: ssrfr selects no algorithms, ciphers or key lengths; TLS parameters are those of the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_working_justification: ssrfr selects no algorithms, ciphers or key lengths; TLS parameters are those of the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_pfs_justification: ssrfr implements no key agreement; TLS key exchange is negotiated by the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_password_storage_justification: ssrfr stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: ssrfr does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: ssrfr selects no algorithms, ciphers or key lengths; TLS parameters are those of the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_used_network_justification: ssrfr fetches the URL its caller supplies, and the default policy allows both http and https. It refuses an https-to-http redirect as a downgrade, and a policy can restrict schemes to https, but plain http is allowed by default.
crypto_tls12_justification: https requests go through libcurl and its TLS backend, which support TLS 1.2 and later; ssrfr never sets or lowers the TLS version: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/R/transport.R
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: ssrfr sets ssl_verifypeer = 1 and ssl_verifyhost = 2 on every transfer and never weakens certificate verification: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/R/transport.R
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: For https, libcurl completes certificate verification in the TLS handshake before any HTTP header is sent, and ssrfr never carries Authorization, Proxy-Authorization or Cookie across an origin on a redirect: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/R/redirect.R
delivery_mitm_justification: ssrfr is installed from GitLab (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr) with remotes::install_gitlab() or pak, over HTTPS only.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Installation fetches sources from GitLab over HTTPS. The project publishes no separate hash or signature files, so no cryptographic hash is served over an unencrypted channel: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items
static_analysis_justification: lintr runs a full-package lint (.lintr, aligned with goodpractice::gp()'s linter set plus locale-safe case-folding rules) as a blocking stage of scripts/verify.R, in the pre-push hook and the verify CI job on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/scripts/verify.R
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check find defects but are not vulnerability scanners, and no vulnerability-focused analyzer or dependency audit job runs over ssrfr (the scheduled renovate job updates dependencies but does not audit them).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: scripts/verify.R fails on any lintr finding, so static-analysis findings are fixed before a push lands.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push: scripts/verify.R is the pre-push hook, and the verify CI job runs it again on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (fuzzer, sanitizer or valgrind) is run. ssrfr is pure R with no compiled code; its testthat, cucumber and conformance-corpus suite runs on every verify, but that is testing, not dynamic analysis.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: ssrfr is pure R with no compiled code (no src/ directory), so it contains no memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: ssrfr's testthat expectations (expect_*) are assertions checked at runtime on every run of the verification chain and the verify CI job: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no findings to fix.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The GitLab CI pipeline (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/pipelines) runs scripts/verify.R (lint, NEWS heading, the test suite with no skips, R CMD check --as-cran) and coverage on every push to main (configuration: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml), plus a weekly scheduled full-check on older R versions. Branch pushes and merge requests start no pipeline; the same chain runs as a pre-push hook on every branch.
discussion_justification: GitLab Issues provide a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed. A gitleaks scan of the full git history (342 commits across all refs, 2026-10-03) reported six findings, all the private keys of the throwaway TLS test fixtures in tests/testthat/certs/: certificates for RFC 2606 .invalid and .example hosts that never resolve, trusted only by the tests, with the CA key discarded (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/blob/main/tests/testthat/certs/make-certs.sh).
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr#readme
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms (e.g. HTTP security headers, compiler hardening flags) apply to web applications and compiled code; ssrfr is a pure-R library.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab) manage their own authentication; ssrfr operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: frequent commits on main toward the first CRAN release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/ssrfr/-/commits/main
